# Airdrops points farming and spam airdrop token safety on Solana

# Airdrops points farming and spam airdrop token safety on Solana — concept pack (small)

> Source-anchored research for Airdrops points farming and spam airdrop token safety on Solana. Run status: COMPLETED.

## Structure and components

- [statement] Investors usually report non-business airdrop income on Schedule 1 (Form 1040). TaxAudit names Part I, line v, 'Digital assets received as ordinary income not reported elsewhere', and CoinLedger says Schedule 1 'Other Income' with a description such as 'crypto airdrop'. The IRS digital-assets page says to report income from forks, staking and mining on Schedule 1, and payments received as an independent contractor on Schedule C. (medium confidence) — https://taxaudit.com/tax-audit-blog/2025/cryptocurrency-airdrop-should-i-report-it-on-my-taxes · keywords: Airdrops points farming and spam airdrop token safety on Solana · also: https://coinledger.io/blog/airdrop-taxes, https://www.irs.gov/filing/digital-assets

## How it works

- [statement] Opaque or shifting conversion rules trigger backlash. EigenLayer's May 2024 airdrop drew criticism for non-transferable tokens, exclusion of users in more than a dozen countries who could still deposit, and unclear treatment of points earned through liquid restaking. Tensor and EigenLayer both revised terms after criticism, and Blur was criticised for extending its points window and changing airdrop rules. Compound's founder called points the largest information asymmetry in crypto. (medium confidence) — https://malaysia.news.yahoo.com/eigenlayers-eigen-airdrop-might-signal-231248249.html · keywords: Airdrops points farming and spam airdrop token safety on Solana · also: https://galaxy.com/insights/research/crypto-points-programs
- [statement] Rewarding raw activity counts attracts farmers. In Optimism's Airdrop 5 the 'Frequent User' bonus (10 or more app transactions a week in at least 20 weeks) cut 30-day retention by 7.1 percentage points, while 'Superchain Explorer' (activity on 7 or more chains) raised it 4.7 points and 'SuperFest Participant' raised it 10.0 points; the authors suspect farmers sell and leave. An academic study of nine airdrops makes the same point: when transaction count is the metric, low fees let farmers hit thresholds cheaply. (medium confidence) — https://gov.optimism.io/t/did-op-airdrop-5-increase-user-retention-rates-a-regression-discontinuity-analysis/9610 · keywords: Airdrops points farming and spam airdrop token safety on Solana · also: https://arxiv.org/html/2312.02752v4
- [statement] Standard practitioner method: the fair market value included as income when the airdrop is received becomes the cost basis, so a later sale is taxed only on the change from that value. The one open-source accounting tool skimmed (Onchain-Accounting) documents the same rule. Record the USD price at the moment of claim or receipt. (medium confidence) — https://tokentax.co/blog/are-unclaimed-crypto-airdrops-taxable · keywords: Airdrops points farming and spam airdrop token safety on Solana · also: https://github.com/Gemma41/Onchain-Accounting/wiki
- [statement] Timing for claim-based and locked airdrops is a vendor interpretation of dominion and control, not IRS guidance. TokenTax says push airdrops are taxable when usable tokens arrive, claim-based airdrops when the claim gives control, and locked tokens after the lockup ends. Unclaimed airdrops are generally not taxed until control exists. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-09-21) — https://tokentax.co/blog/are-unclaimed-crypto-airdrops-taxable
- [statement] For UK airdrops not taxed as income, base cost is uncertain. Recap reports no HMRC guidance on acquisition cost and suggests nil cost when tokens are issued directly to the recipient. For income-taxed airdrops, receipt-date market value is the acquisition cost. (medium confidence) — https://docs.recap.io/uk-tax-guide-for-individuals/transaction-types/airdrops · keywords: Airdrops points farming and spam airdrop token safety on Solana · also: https://www.gov.uk/hmrc-internal-manuals/cryptoassets-manual/crypto21250
- [statement] No IRS rule fixes the timing for claim-based or locked airdrops beyond the dominion-and-control test. TokenTax reads the test this way: a push airdrop is income when usable tokens arrive; a claim-based airdrop is income when the claim gives control; a locked token is income when the lock ends; an unclaimed allocation is not income while the holder lacks control; and a claim made years later uses the claim-date value. Koinly says the IRS has not clarified whether income arises when an airdrop becomes available or when it is claimed. TokenTax adds that constructive receipt can apply if the tokens were already unconditionally available before a simple administrative step. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-09-21) — https://tokentax.co/blog/are-unclaimed-crypto-airdrops-taxable · keywords: Airdrops points farming and spam airdrop token safety on Solana · also: https://koinly.io/blog/crypto-airdrop-tax/, https://www.irs.gov/irb/2019-44_IRB
- [statement] Timing rules for push, claim-based and locked airdrops are interpretations of dominion and control, not IRS rules. TokenTax says a push airdrop is taxable when usable tokens arrive, a claim-based airdrop when the claim gives control, and a locked token when the lock ends; unclaimed allocations are generally not taxed. CoinLedger says the IRS has not said whether income arises when an airdrop becomes available or when it is claimed, and expects a dominion-and-control test. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-09-21) — https://tokentax.co/blog/are-unclaimed-crypto-airdrops-taxable · keywords: Airdrops points farming and spam airdrop token safety on Solana · also: https://coinledger.io/blog/airdrop-taxes

## Measurements and reference values

- [statement] Jito's validator and searcher allocations were 50% claimable at genesis and 50% vesting linearly over 12 months. Claims were valid for 18 months, with unclaimed tokens returning to the DAO treasury. (low confidence) — https://www.chaincatcher.com/en/article/2107694

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] Scoping the 'airdrops fail' headline: after Arbitrum's airdrop, unique addresses stayed about 50% above pre-airdrop levels and TVL rose over 50% without a significant drop, but per-address transaction counts fell to under 75% of pre-airdrop. The authors call airdrops possibly necessary to attract users initially but insufficient to build a committed community. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2312.02752v4
- [statement] TokenTax says the One Big Beautiful Bill Act made the elimination of miscellaneous itemized deductions permanent after 2025, so a hobby-classified farmer cannot deduct gas, VPN or hardware costs against airdrop income; its example is $10,000 of income and $3,000 of costs, all taxed. Chief Counsel Advice 202302011 confirms only that section 67(g) suspended these deductions for 2018 through 2025. The permanence claim has one source; check the statute before relying on it. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-05) — https://tokentax.co/blog/airdrop-farming-taxes · keywords: Airdrops points farming and spam airdrop token safety on Solana · also: https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-wd/202302011.pdf
- [statement] The Tax Institute of Australia argues that draft TR 2026/D1 (Example 5, paragraphs 47-51) treats unsolicited tokens as received property without asking whether the recipient knew of them, assented to them, could exclude others or could transact with them. It says malicious, frozen, non-transferable, inaccessible and unmarketable tokens cannot all be treated as immediately owned and valuable because a ledger entry exists, and asks the ATO to address awareness, control and practical capacity before imposing income inclusion or a market-value cost base. It also asks the ATO to wait for the High Court's judgment in Poulton v Conrad, then reserved. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-16) — https://www.taxinstitute.com.au/content/dam/thetaxinstitute/resources/submissions/2026/26%2010%2016%20TTI%20submission%20-%20ATO%20consultation%20on%20TD%202026%20D2%20and%20TR%202026%20D1%20-%20For%20publication.pdf · keywords: Airdrops points farming and spam airdrop token safety on Solana · also: https://www.taxinstitute.com.au/resources/submissions/2026/ato-consultation-on-td-2026-d2-and-tr-2026-d1
- [statement] Tax tools bake in jurisdiction-specific defaults about airdrops, so a US filer cannot trust them unchecked. BittyTax (UK-focused) records its Airdrop type as not taxed as income because nothing is assumed done in return, and says to use Income when a service or condition applied; its README does not address spam. ChainLedger (Solana, EVM and Cosmos; built for Indian fiscal years) moves 'spam, dust, and airdrops' into an excluded CSV with a reason. Onchain-Accounting values airdrops at the receipt-date fiat rate and uses that value as basis. Review tool classifications against the control-and-value test. (medium confidence) — https://github.com/BittyTax/BittyTax · keywords: Airdrops points farming and spam airdrop token safety on Solana · also: https://github.com/vitwit/chainledger, https://github.com/Gemma41/Onchain-Accounting/wiki
- [statement] Vendors say losses from an airdrop scam usually cannot be deducted. TaxAudit says personal theft losses, meaning losses not connected with a trade or business, a for-profit investment or a federally declared disaster, were generally nondeductible for 2018 through 2025 under the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act and may stay so if that act is extended. CoinLedger says such casualty losses typically can't be deducted. Their status after 2025 was not checked against a primary source. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-01-02) — https://taxaudit.com/tax-audit-blog/2025/cryptocurrency-airdrop-should-i-report-it-on-my-taxes · keywords: Airdrops points farming and spam airdrop token safety on Solana · also: https://coinledger.io/blog/airdrop-taxes

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] Do not interact with an unsolicited token only to dispose of it for tax purposes. TokenTax advises seeking tax advice for a material amount rather than interacting with an unknown smart contract to effect a disposal. KoinX says never to click token links, swap, transfer or connect a wallet to claim an unknown token, and to hide or mark it as spam instead. Koinly warns that any action involving a worthless spam token may lead to a loss of funds. (medium confidence) — https://tokentax.co/blog/are-unclaimed-crypto-airdrops-taxable · keywords: Airdrops points farming and spam airdrop token safety on Solana · also: https://www.koinx.com/tax-guides/spam-tokens-in-crypto, https://support.koinly.io/en/articles/9490057-spam-tokens

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Projects use points before a token exists to steer user behaviour. Rewarded actions seen on Solana include trading volume and PnL, lending and borrowing, liquidity provision, referrals, asset boosts, and not listing NFTs on rival marketplaces. Points need no fixed emissions schedule, so the team can retune rates between seasons. (medium confidence) — https://threesigma.xyz/blog/point-programs · keywords: Airdrops points farming and spam airdrop token safety on Solana · also: https://galaxy.com/insights/research/crypto-points-programs
- [statement] Solana points programs write anti-gaming rules into the criteria: Tensor Season 1 required at least 500 SOL of NFT trading volume and banned wash trading; Tensor Season 2 rewarded loyalty (not listing on other marketplaces); Parcl can revoke points from self-referrals; Kamino limits LST-only or stablecoin-only farming. Points can also distort behaviour: Zeta users felt pushed into market orders and took slippage. (medium confidence) — https://threesigma.xyz/blog/point-programs · keywords: Airdrops points farming and spam airdrop token safety on Solana · also: https://galaxy.com/insights/research/crypto-points-programs
- [statement] Jito excluded all past and current core contributors, including core-contributor wallets holding JitoSOL, validators they operate and canary searchers they operate. Recipients had 18 months from the token generation date to claim; after that, unclaimed JTO moves permissionlessly to the DAO treasury's Realms wallet. (medium confidence) — https://www.jito.network/blog/jto-airdrop-eligibility-and-allocation-specifications · keywords: Airdrops points farming and spam airdrop token safety on Solana · also: https://www.chaincatcher.com/en/article/2107694
- [statement] Tax tools handle spam by exclusion. In Koinly, marking a token as spam deletes all transactions with that token, hides its balances, and applies to future imports. Koinly advises this for tokens that arrived unsolicited, were never touched and are worthless, and says it does not know which options your country allows. The open-source ChainLedger exporter, which supports Solana, writes spam, dust and airdrops to an excluded CSV with a reason for each row. KoinX warns that manipulated liquidity pools can give spam tokens inflated prices that distort reported income if they are not flagged. Exclusion is a bookkeeping step, not a legal finding. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-02) — https://support.koinly.io/en/articles/9490057-spam-tokens · keywords: Airdrops points farming and spam airdrop token safety on Solana · also: https://github.com/vitwit/chainledger, https://www.koinx.com/tax-guides/spam-tokens-in-crypto
- [statement] Koinly says a dust attack, in which a scammer sends tiny deposits of a legitimate token such as SOL, should not be marked as spam. It advises tagging the deposits as Airdrop or Reward instead, and aggregating them if they arrive daily. The amounts can be so small that they display as zero. (low confidence) (verified as of 2025-12-31) — https://support.koinly.io/en/articles/9490057-spam-tokens
- [statement] Tax tools make airdrop income a setting. Koinly has a 'treat airdrops as income?' switch for users in countries where airdrops are income. The open-source Onchain-Accounting app values staking, airdrop and interest income at the fiat rate on the receipt date and carries that value into the asset's cost basis, which matches the US basis rule. (medium confidence) — https://koinly.io/blog/crypto-airdrop-tax/ · keywords: Airdrops points farming and spam airdrop token safety on Solana · also: https://github.com/Gemma41/Onchain-Accounting/wiki
- [statement] Paschall carries limited weight. EY notes it is a memorandum opinion on a fully stipulated record with a pro se taxpayer and no expert testimony, that the court did not rely on IRS administrative guidance and declined to address a Loper Bright challenge, and that taxpayers without dominion and control over staked tokens may reach a different result. (low confidence) — https://taxnews.ey.com/news/2026-1297-tax-court-confirms-staking-rewards-are-taxable-upon-receipt
